remaining: Tatra banka only - tatrabanka.sk is fully Cloudflare-blocked and Claude-in-Chrome was unavailable; escalated as an operator request.

signals.signal: SLSP's H1-2026 KPI table shows the ATM fleet SHRANK from 752 at 31/12/2025 to 733 at 30/06/2026 (-2.5%, -19 machines) while the branch network fell from 140 to 128 (-8.5%, -12 branches) over the same six months. Headcount fell 3,642 to 3,589; issued cards rose 1,909k to 1,941k; internet-banking users 1,397k to 1,414k.
signals.source_name: Slovenska sporitelna press release 'Hospodarske vysledky Slovenskej sporitelne k 30. junu 2026' (PDF), table 'Vybrane ukazovatele obchodnej cinnosti'
signals.implies: Branches are closing roughly four times faster than ATMs, so cash service has to migrate onto self-service. That is precisely the deposit/recycling-ATM and assisted-service-kiosk substitution Printec sells, plus a managed-services wrap to run a consolidating estate at lower cost per machine.
signals.likelihood: High that branch and ATM consolidation continues through 2026-27 at the observed run-rate
signals.followup: Model displaced cash transactions per closed branch and take SLSP a recycler-per-closed-branch business case; re-pull the KPI table at FY-2026 to date the trend.

signals.signal: SLSP's H1-2026 infographic states '746 bankomatov vratane 250 vkladomatov' (746 ATMs including 250 deposit ATMs), self-described as the largest network in Slovakia. NOTE the discrepancy with the same-day KPI table, which gives 733 ATMs at 30/06/2026. On either figure only about a third of the estate is deposit-capable, leaving roughly 480-500 cash-out-only machines.
signals.source_name: Slovenska sporitelna, 'SLSP v cislach - 1. polrok 2026' infographic (PDF)
signals.implies: Roughly 480-500 cash-out-only ATMs at the country's largest bank form the directly addressable base for Printec deposit modules and recyclers. The 746-vs-733 gap must be resolved before either number is quoted to a client.
signals.likelihood: Medium - deposit share is only a third of the fleet and the direction of travel is upward
signals.followup: Ask SLSP IR to reconcile 746 vs 733 (partner or white-label machines?); pull the 'Aktualny zoznam vkladovych bankomatov' list from slsp.sk to geo-map the 250 deposit sites and expose the upgrade backlog.

signals.signal: SLSP's deposit-ATM product page states coins cannot be deposited ('Mince sa cez vkladomat nedaju vlozit'); only EUR 5-500 banknotes, max 200 notes per deposit, max EUR 20,000 per account per day. Contactless deposit works only at selected machines.
signals.implies: Coin handling is complete white space in Slovak self-service - the 'ATM 2.0 coin' proposition (coin deposit and recycling modules, coin kiosks) has no incumbent at the largest bank. 'Selected machines' for contactless deposit also flags a partly older estate due a refresh.
signals.likelihood: Low-Medium inside 6-12 months - no announced coin programme, but SME and retail coin float is unaddressed in a mature euro market
signals.followup: Test appetite with the SLSP Biznis cash-handling team; quantify SME coin volumes currently forced into the 128 remaining branches.

signals.signal: VUB's deposit-ATM page states the bank has 150 ATMs with a deposit function; banknotes only (EUR 5-500), coins explicitly excluded ('mince cez bankomat nie je mozne vkladat'), and per-deposit capacity is either 50 or 200 notes depending on the ATM model.
signals.source_name: VUB banka - 'Vkladovy bankomat & vkladomat' product page
signals.implies: The 50-note vs 200-note split is a hardware-generation tell: the 50-note machines are prime refresh candidates for Printec recyclers. Coins are excluded here too, confirming the coin white space across the market's top banks. VUB's 150 deposit ATMs are well behind SLSP's 250.
signals.likelihood: Medium - a mixed-generation estate normally forces a refresh decision inside 12-24 months, and VUB is visibly behind the market leader
signals.followup: Obtain VUB's TOTAL ATM count to compute the non-deposit remainder (locator API blocked this run - try the mobile app endpoints or ask VUB directly).

signals.signal: VUB's H1-2026 semi-annual financial report states the group had 163 business outlets across Slovakia at 30/06/2026 (retail branches, corporate branches and mortgage centres) - EXACTLY unchanged from 163 at 31/12/2025 - plus one branch in Czechia. Group headcount fell to 3,179 from 3,215; bank-only headcount 3,151 from 3,187. The report discloses no ATM or POS figure.
signals.source_name: VUB, a.s. - Polrocna financna sprava za rok 2026 (H1-2026 semi-annual financial report, PDF)
signals.implies: VUB is holding its physical network flat while SLSP cuts 8.5% of branches in six months. That is a different sales story: VUB is not substituting branches with machines, so the pitch is in-branch cash automation and teller-cash recyclers to lower the cost of a network it has chosen to keep - the same play the baseline identified at CEC Bank in Romania.
signals.likelihood: Medium - a flat network under falling headcount usually means automation inside the branch
signals.followup: Pitch teller-assist and back-office cash recyclers for the 163 retained outlets; check the FY-2026 report for whether the flat network holds.

signals.entity: Financne riaditelstvo SR / entire Slovak merchant base (eKasa)
signals.signal: Act No. 384/2025 Coll. on Revenue Recording took effect 01/01/2026, replacing the previous eKasa regime, and has already been amended by Act No. 30/2026 Coll. effective 28/02/2026. Section 15 obliges every seller using an eKasa register to let the buyer pay cashlessly on any sale exceeding EUR 1; the transitional provision applies that duty FROM 01/05/2026. The only exemptions are no internet signal at the point of sale, or an outage of the technical means supplied by the state or a third party.
signals.source_name: Slov-lex, Zbierka zakonov SR - Act 384/2025 Coll., consolidated text effective 28/02/2026 (static portal mirror)
signals.implies: A universal statutory card/electronic acceptance mandate, live since 01/05/2026 across the whole Slovak merchant base - the single largest POS-terminal and acquiring-integration trigger in this market, directly analogous to the Albanian POS/POI obligation in the baseline. Maps to Printec POS/acquiring plus managed services.
signals.likelihood: Already in force - the live variable over the next 6-12 months is the enforcement ramp
signals.followup: Size the un-terminalised merchant tail (micro-merchants and market traders - FR SR publishes a dedicated 'pomocka pre jarmocnikov a predajcov na trhu'); pitch SoftPOS or low-cost POS bundled with Printec's already-certified eKasa Service.

signals.entity: Financne riaditelstvo SR / entire Slovak merchant base (eKasa)
signals.signal: Act 384/2025 s.15(3) provides that the Financial Directorate supplies the technical means letting an eKasa register obtain confirmation of a QR-code-initiated cashless payment - and expressly states that 'technicke prostriedky moze poskytovat aj tretia strana' (a third party may also provide those technical means). Penalties under ss.16-17 reach EUR 3,000-40,000 per repeat breach for the most serious offences and EUR 300-13,000 for lesser ones, with a warning only on first detection.
signals.source_name: Slov-lex, Zbierka zakonov SR - Act 384/2025 Coll., ss.15-17, consolidated text effective 28/02/2026
signals.implies: An explicit statutory opening for a private vendor to operate the payment-confirmation layer between POS and the fiscal system. Printec could position a certified third-party confirmation service alongside its existing eKasa certification. The fine bands give merchants a hard compliance ROI to quote in the sales conversation.
signals.likelihood: Medium - conditional on FR SR publishing the technical specification for third-party providers
signals.followup: Watch financnasprava.sk for the published technical specification of the QR-payment-confirmation means and whether third parties must be accredited.

signals.signal: An FR SR notice on the eKasa portal states that the s.11(4) duty to report eKasa register faults is NOT currently applied, because the technical solution will only be delivered within a NEW revenue-recording system called SAFE, whose entry into operation 'sa nepredpoklada v roku 2026' (is not expected in 2026).
signals.source_name: Financna sprava SR - eKasa portal, notice on reporting eKasa register faults under s.11(4) of Act 384/2025
signals.implies: A full national fiscalisation-platform replacement is coming with go-live pushed beyond 2026. Every certified cash-register program and protected data store in Slovakia will need re-integration and probably re-certification - a multi-year POS/ORP replacement and integration wave that an already-certified vendor is positioned to capture.
signals.likelihood: High that SAFE lands in 2027-28; the regulator itself rules out 2026
signals.followup: Track SAFE procurement notices on FR SR and the Slovak public-procurement journal (UVO); get onto the FR SR integrator consultation list before the specification freezes.

signals.entity: PRINTEC SLOVAKIA spol. s r.o. (own incumbency) vs DIEBOLD NIXDORF s.r.o.
signals.signal: On the FR SR register of valid eKasa certification decisions as at 19/08/2026, PRINTEC SLOVAKIA spol. s r.o. (Elektrarenska 4, 831 04 Bratislava, ICO 35 702 044) holds decision no. 322095/2025 dated 20/06/2025 certifying 'Printec eKasa Service verzia 1.2' with SwissBit F6 protected data storage as an on-line registracna pokladnica. DIEBOLD NIXDORF s.r.o. Bratislava holds decision 284623/2025 dated 03/06/2025 for 'DNSK PPEKK v2.2 / DNSK CHDU v2.1'. Certification decisions are valid for at most 5 years.
signals.source_name: Financna sprava SR - 'Zoznam platnych rozhodnuti o certifikacii pokladnicnych programov a chranenych datovych ulozisk k 19.08.2026' (PDF)
signals.implies: Printec already holds the regulatory licence to sell fiscalised POS into the s.15 acceptance mandate - a ready-made go-to-market asset most competitors lack. Diebold Nixdorf is the named head-to-head competitor on the same register. Printec's certification runs to roughly 20/06/2030.
signals.likelihood: Immediate - the certification is live now and the acceptance mandate is already in force
signals.followup: Confirm internally how many Printec eKasa Service units are deployed versus the certified competitor set; plan re-certification well before June 2030 and for the SAFE migration.

signals.entity: Financne riaditelstvo SR / eKasa hardware lifecycle
signals.signal: FR SR's 'Vyrobcovia eKasy' page sets out three recurring forced-replacement events: eKasa client authentication credentials expire 2 years after issue; the protected data store (CHDU) fills within an estimated 2-6 years depending on capacity and must then be swapped; and a certification decision is valid for at most 5 years from taking legal effect.
signals.implies: The Slovak fiscal regime builds a guaranteed recurring hardware-swap and credential-renewal cycle into the whole merchant base - an annuity-shaped managed-services and consumables revenue stream, not a one-off box sale.
signals.likelihood: Certain - these are standing statutory and technical lifecycles
signals.followup: Build a CHDU-replacement and credential-renewal managed service around the installed base of Printec eKasa Service units.

signals.signal: NBS convened a national conference on online fraud and announced the launch of a joint coordination platform hosted within an existing Ministry of Interior structure, plus a Single Point of Contact network across banks, telecoms operators, police, the Prosecutor General, the media-services regulator, ESET, the European Commission (DG HOME) and Eurojust. NBS frames online fraud as a systemic risk, citing the forthcoming EU anti-fraud strategy's emphasis on rapid information exchange.
signals.source_name: Narodna banka Slovenska press release - 'Ako spolocne zastavit online podvody - NBS spusta platformu na koordinaciu vsetkych klucovych institucii'
signals.implies: A regulator-led push for cross-institution fraud data sharing normally pulls forward bank spend on transaction monitoring and real-time fraud scoring - Printec's transaction-monitoring and AML/compliance lines. Both SLSP (21/07/2026 and 04/02/2026 fraud warnings) and NBS are actively campaigning on authorised-push-payment fraud.
signals.likelihood: Medium over 6-12 months as the platform moves from conference to operating model
signals.followup: Track whether the Ministry of Interior platform produces a technical data-sharing specification banks must implement; that specification would be the concrete procurement trigger.

coverage_notes: The session's WebSearch budget was already exhausted (200/200) before this subagent started, so ALL research was done by direct fetch against primary domains (curl with a desktop User-Agent, cookie jar and full header set) plus local PDF text extraction with pdfminer.six. Four distinct angles were used, deliberately varied from a locator-count-only approach: (1) bank product pages read for deposit-ATM technical SPECIFICATIONS rather than counts - which is what surfaced the coin exclusion and the 50-note/200-note hardware-generation split; (2) bank H1-2026 results PDFs for the hard KPI tables, which caught the SLSP 746-vs-733 contradiction; (3) the Slovak statute book via Slov-lex's static mirror, which produced the dated s.15 acceptance mandate and the third-party provision; (4) the tax administration's own CERTIFICATION REGISTER, a source type not used in previous runs, which produced verified Printec incumbency and a named competitor. Genuine gaps: Tatra banka was not researched at all (see access_issues and operator_requests); no VUB total ATM count exists in any primary disclosure found; no Slovak national ATM/POS fleet census was obtainable because the NBS payment-card page has not been updated since 2021; no OptiCash or APTRA vendor evidence for Slovakia was found in primary sources this run, so the OptiCash/APTRA focus item is unresolved rather than negative. RBI's H1-2026 semi-annual report was opened and searched - it contains no ATM, branch or Tatra banka fleet figures for Slovakia, only that IT expenses and fixed-asset depreciation rose notably in Slovakia.
access_issues: BLOCKED: www.tatrabanka.sk returns a Cloudflare interstitial (HTTP 403, 'Just a moment...') on every path attempted - /, /sk/, /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml, /sk/o-banke/pre-media/, /sk/personal/ucty-platby/vkladovy-bankomat/ - via WebFetch and via curl with a desktop User-Agent, sk-SK Accept-Language, compression and a cookie jar. Escalation to Claude-in-Chrome was attempted and failed: the Chrome extension is not connected in this environment. Tatra banka is therefore genuinely unresearched, not quiet. BLOCKED: VUB's ATM locator endpoints - https://www.vub.sk/branchLocatorWithMockServlet/ returns only a city list regardless of the operation parameter, and https://www.vub.sk/digitalServicesServlet/ returns statusCode 500 or null to both GET and POST - so no machine-readable VUB ATM feed was obtained. STALE: https://nbs.sk/platby/platobne-nastroje/platobne-karty/ carries no current ATM or POS series; its most recent figure is 5.5m payment cards at 31/12/2021. JS-GATED: www.slov-lex.sk main portal requires JavaScript - resolved by using its own documented static mirror at /static/SK/ZZ/2025/384/20260228.html. NOT AVAILABLE: WebSearch (session budget 200/200 exhausted before this task began).
operator_requests: 1) TATRA BANKA - Cloudflare-blocked to all automated fetching. An operator with a normal browser should capture: (a) https://www.tatrabanka.sk/sk/o-banke/pre-media/ for the H1-2026 / Q2-2026 results release and any ATM or branch KPI table; (b) the Tatra banka deposit-ATM ('vkladovy bankomat') product page for deposit-capable count, note-capacity limits and whether coins are accepted; (c) the branch-and-ATM locator for total and deposit-capable machine counts. 2) VUB TOTAL ATM COUNT - not disclosed in the H1-2026 report and the locator API is dead; an operator should read the count off the live locator at https://www.vub.sk/ludia/pobocky-bankomaty.html, or capture the XHR the map makes, so the 150 deposit ATMs can be expressed as a share of the fleet.
